detail: Wrong from the first step: solved YTM as 4.7174% instead of 4.6867% (+3.07 bp). Duration, convexity, and exact reprice all inherit the error. Model's own closing explanation blamed 'Macaulay vs modified duration confusion' rather than the actual root cause — a numerically wrong YTM solve.

Started wrong (158.41 bp, modified duration 1.5825y — annual-compounding divisor on a semi-annual bond, the inverse of this project's original bug) but caught it unprompted mid-answer, named the actual mechanism (wrong compounding divisor, not Taylor truncation), recalculated with the periodic-yield divisor, and landed within tolerance. Same model family that produced the original bug two weeks ago; this run self-corrected instead of rationalizing.

Clean, correct on the first pass, no self-correction needed. Every intermediate value matches the verified reference exactly: YTM 4.6867357%, accrued interest 19.5652, dirty price 997.5652, Macaulay 3.242814, modified duration 3.168563, convexity 12.16778. Explicitly named the diagnostic: a gap of several bp would point to a wrong duration/convexity or accrual convention, not Taylor truncation — matching this project's own framing.

Clean YTM solve: correctly set up the bisection with the 4/184-period stub for the first coupon and matched the reference to 5 decimal places. Consistent with the same model's clean fi-010 pass — the accrued interest and cash-flow timing this bond needs were already worked out correctly there.

Off by 0.51 bp — well within the wider band added specifically for this case. Accrued interest and dirty price were both exact, so the divergence is purely in how far the yield solver iterated, not a conceptual error. This is the exact same value an earlier Haiku 4.5 session gave for this identical bond two weeks ago: two independent runs converging on 4.6918% suggests this is a recognizable stopping point for this model's YTM iteration, not random noise, even though it doesn't rise to a full known_failure_mode entry yet.

Off by 3.07 bp — outside even the wider near-miss band. The identical 4.7174% this same model derived independently in the earlier fi-010 run, from a full worked table (semi-annual rate, annualized nominal, and effective annual, all internally consistent with each other but all ~3 bp off the true rate). Two independent runs landing on the exact same wrong figure is a stronger signal than either result alone: this looks like a systematic bias in how this model solves the yield equation, not one-off noise.

Carried forward the same wrong YTM as its fi-001 near-miss (4.6918% instead of 4.6867%), but modified duration is not very sensitive to a 0.5 bp yield error, so the final duration lands inside tolerance anyway. Passes on this problem despite the upstream figure being off — this problem alone would not have caught it.
Clean throughout: correct YTM (4.6867357%), correct Macaulay (3.2428136), correct modified duration division by (1 + y/2). Matches the reference to 5 decimal places.

Same systematic YTM bias as the fi-001 and fi-010 runs (y/2 = 2.3587%, i.e. y = 4.7174% again — third independent occurrence of this exact wrong figure), but here it produces only a 0.019-year gap, landing as a near miss rather than a clean fail. Notable finding: the same underlying wrong YTM is 'near miss' on duration but was 'badly wrong' (27.85 bp vs 0.09 bp expected) on fi-010's scenario residual — how much a fixed upstream error matters depends heavily on which downstream quantity is asked for.
